source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Identify affected devices and follow recall-specific correction or removal instructions and facility policy","B":"Discard every recalled device permanently because all FDA recalls require product removal or destruction","C":"Continue using every recalled device until it fails because recall notices are informational only","D":"Ignore the recall unless a patient has already been injured by the exact affected device in use"}}
source_row.rationale: FDA defines a medical-device recall as a correction or removal action. A recall does not always require stopping use or returning the device; some recalls require inspection, adjustment, repair, labeling changes, or other correction. The facility should identify affected inventory and follow the specific recall instructions and its internal response process.
source_row.source_detail: Current FDA page: a recall may involve correction or removal; it does not always mean the product must be stopped or returned and can require checking, adjusting, or fixing the device.
source_row.source_name: FDA — What Is a Medical Device Recall?
source_row.stem: A hospital receives an FDA medical-device recall notice for equipment currently in use. What is the most appropriate initial facility response?
